from sklearn.naive_bayes import MultinomialNB
from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import CountVectorizer

docs = ["team wins match", "player scores goal", "debate election policy"]
y = [1, 1, 0]
vec = CountVectorizer()
X = vec.fit_transform(docs)
nb = MultinomialNB()
nb.fit(X, y)
print(nb.predict(vec.transform(["goal win team"])))

fit_transform learns the vocabulary and encodes the training documents as counts. You fit MultinomialNB with those counts and labels.
